reconcile.note: John Gill treats the threatened scattering as a conditional punishment for idolatry, culminating in the Assyrian and Babylonian captivities, not a cancelled promise.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells sets the promise that Abraham's seed would be as the stars of heaven against Deuteronomy's threat that they would be left few in number, calling it a contradiction.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (1999-2013), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Will there be many Jews?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/jews_many.html).

sides.snippet: in multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and as the sand which is on the seashore.
sides.verseText: that in blessing I will bless you, and in multiplying I will multiply your seed as the stars of the heavens, and as the sand which is on the seashore. Your seed will possess the gate of his enemies.

sides.snippet: Yahweh will scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the nations, where Yahweh shall lead you away.
sides.verseText: Yahweh will scatter you among the peoples, and you shall be left few in number among the nations, where Yahweh shall lead you away.
